events.content:
Both routes render correctly (the non-zero exit is just from killing the server afterwards). Everything is in place.

## What I did

This is Next.js 16.4-canary, which ships React's `<ViewTransition>` API in its default bundled React channel and has first-class support via `<Link transitionTypes>` — so no experimental config flag or third-party library was needed. Changes:

**Shared element morph** — The grid thumbnail in `app/ProductGrid.tsx` and the detail hero in `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` are each wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`}>`. Because the names match across pages, React pairs them during navigation and the browser morphs the thumbnail into the hero (position, size, and aspect ratio animate). Names are only assigned during an actual transition, so there's no per-element `view-transition-name` overhead at rest.

**Directional page slides** — The root layout (`app/layout.tsx`) wraps `{children}` in a `<ViewTransition>` whose `default` prop maps transition types to CSS classes. Grid→detail links pass `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` and the back link passes `['nav-back']`; Next feeds these to `React.addTransitionType` during the navigation. In `globals.css`, `::view-transition-old/new(*.page-slide-forward)` slides the old page out left and the new page in from the right, and `*.page-slide-back` does the reverse. Untyped navigations (e.g. the browser back button) fall through to a plain cross-fade.

**Suspense transitions** — Both Suspense boundaries (the product grid and the product details panel) are wrapped in `<ViewTransition default="content-fade">`, so the skeleton→content reveal animates as a 200ms cross-fade instead of popping in.

**Reduced motion** — A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements, which makes every transition (slides, morphs, fades) complete instantly while content still swaps correctly. It also stops the skeleton pulse animation.

I also added `react-canary.d.ts` with `/// <reference types="react/canary" />` so TypeScript picks up the `ViewTransition` and `transitionTypes` typings from `@types/react`. Verified with a clean `tsc --noEmit`, a successful production build, and a smoke test confirming both routes return 200 with the expected markup.
